trap-superlative.evidence: Two unqualified universals that the block's own text undercuts. (1) 'The pure number ratio $v/m_e \approx 4.8\times10^5$ derives strictly from topology.' - but v/m_e = N_v/3, and the block's own 'Open computations' section opens by saying N_v 'must be derived ... from the Skein algebra'. The ratio is asserted to be derived in one section and listed as underived two sections later. (2) 'Every standard-physics constant decomposes into $q$-dependent factors times $\mu_0$' - a universal over all of physics, supported by three examples, one of which (v) is the open item above and another of which (alpha) is quoted with an error figure that matches no route in the chapter (see notes).
trap-superlative.notes: Structural (factual scoping), not edited. Proposed fix for (1): 'The pure number ratio v/m_e = N_v/3 is fixed once N_v is derived from the Skein algebra; that derivation is open (below).' For (2): 'The constants entering the half-life formula decompose into q-dependent factors times mu_0:' - drop 'Every standard-physics'. THREE NUMERIC/CONTENT ITEMS REPORTED SEPARATELY: (a) the '2.1 ppm deviation from CODATA' matches NOTHING - recomputed, the bare alpha = q^{-1}/([9]_q[10]_q) quoted in that very sentence is off by 1553 ppm, the Chern-Simons-corrected value by 0.399 ppm, the fixed-point cubic by 0.0007 ppm and the PSLQ form by 0.003-0.006 ppm; the nearest thing in the corpus is the additive Bring zero-mode residual of -4.2 ppm, of which 2.1 is exactly half. The same sentence also attributes the BARE formula to 'the Chern-Simons correction', which is a second mismatch. (b) PARAMETER RELABELLING: 'the Fermi constant is not an independent parameter' holds only because G_F is re-expressed through N_v = v/(E_x mu_0), and N_v is undetermined - so one free input has been renamed, not eliminated, and v approx 246 GeV is an experimental input outside CAL-1/2/3. (c) SYMBOL COLLISION: 's' is used here for a crossing asymmetry vanishing at q=1, while prop:golden-skew-dual-node and its proof use s = sqrt(q), which equals 1 at q=1. Also '10-17% overshoot in heavy-nucleus half-life predictions' carries no witness or citation.
